PTDF unveils strategy to support Nigeria’s $1trn GDP target
items.description: By Obas Esiedesa, Abuja The Petroleum Technology Development Fund (PTDF) has unveiled a human capital development strategy aimed at supporting the Federal Government’s target of growing Nigeria’s economy to $1 trillion by 2030 through investment in specialised education, technical skills and energy research. The Executive Secretary of PTDF, Prof. Shua’ibu Aliyu, disclosed this on Friday in Kaduna, saying the Fund was aligning its programmes with the 2026–2030 National Development Plan to develop a highly skilled workforce capable of driving growth across Nigeria’s oil, gas and emerging energy sectors. Aliyu said the strategy focuses on building local capacity, reducing capital flight, strengthening research institutions and providing the manpower required for major energy infrastructure projects. “Our long-term vision is to develop a workforce that is trained in Nigeria, employed in Nigeria, and, by choice, exported to serve the broader African energy industry,” he said. He explained that the initiative would be implemented through two flagship institutions — the Centre for Skills Development and Training in Port Harcourt and the newly renamed General Shehu Musa Yar’Adua University of Geological Science and Engineering Technology in Kaduna. According to him, the Port Harcourt centre would provide internationally recognised vocational and technical training for technicians, artisans and craftsmen in the upstream, midstream and downstream petroleum sectors, with certifications in areas such as welding, fabrication, instrumentation and offshore safety. He added that the Kaduna-based university, recently licensed by the National Universities Commission (NUC) to operate as a postgraduate institution, would provide advanced education and research opportunities through partnerships with leading universities in the United Kingdom. Aliyu described the institution as “a strategic catalyst for Nigeria’s economic growth” through the development of local technical expertise and conservation of foreign exchange. To reduce dependence on overseas education, the PTDF boss said the Fund had expanded its split-site doctoral programme, allowing scholars to complete part of their studies in Nigeria and the remainder at partner universities abroad. “This initiative reduces capital flight while strengthening local institutions and maintaining international academic standards,” he said. He disclosed that PTDF was also digitising the university to improve administrative efficiency and support blended learning. The Executive Secretary said the Fund had aligned its training programmes with major national energy projects, including the AKK Gas Pipeline, UTM Floating LNG, Trans-Saharan Gas Pipeline, Bonga Southwest Aparo, Owowo, Zabazaba-Etan, OB3 Gas Trunk Line, Olokola LNG, Dangote projects and other investments by indigenous operators. He said the move was aimed at ensuring Nigeria develops the skilled workforce needed to execute future investments across the energy value chain. Aliyu added that PTDF was strengthening international partnerships with organisations such as the Independent Petroleum Producers Group, African Petroleum Producers’ Organization (APPO), Sonatrach of Algeria, Saudi Aramco and Turkish Petroleum to promote knowledge transfer, research and innovation. To reposition its academic institutions, he said PTDF had inaugurated a nine-member committee to review the university system, assess governance, infrastructure, research capacity, digital systems and academic programmes, and recommend reforms that would transform the institution into a globally competitive centre of excellence in petroleum, energy and strategic technology. The PTDF chief attributed the Fund’s achievements to the support of President Bola Tinubu, particularly the recent renaming of the university, which he said demonstrated the administration’s commitment to developing Nigeria’s energy workforce. Chairman of the review committee, Dr Omar Farouk Ibrahim, assured that the panel would carry out its assignment diligently and provide recommendations capable of transforming the institution. items.title: 2027: APC has failed Nigerians, ADC chieftain tells Tinubu, Mbah
items.description: By Anayo Okoli ENUGU — A chieftain of the African Democratic Congress (ADC) in Enugu State, Dr. (Sir) Walter Oji, has criticised the All Progressives Congress (APC) administration, alleging that the party has failed Nigerians and would struggle to secure victory in the 2027 general elections. Oji, a Fourth Degree Knight of the Catholic Church, made the remarks during the inaugural meeting of the G24 for Atiku Abubakar and Ocho Obodoeze 2027 Movement, an ADC support group, in Enugu. He claimed that the APC-led government had worsened economic hardship, insecurity and poverty in the country, arguing that Nigerians would demand a change of leadership in 2027. According to him, the ruling party had not delivered enough to justify another term in office. “It is time to tell Bola Tinubu that Nigerians deserve a new direction and that Alhaji Atiku Abubakar, a man with experience in governance and economic management, should be given the opportunity to lead the country in 2027,” Oji said. He also criticised Enugu State Governor Peter Mbah’s administration, alleging that some of its policies had increased the economic burden on residents. Oji urged residents of the state to support the ADC governorship candidate, Chief Ocho Obodoeze, ahead of the 2027 election. “I urge the people of Enugu State to support a new vision that prioritises development, prosperity and good governance,” he said. The ADC chieftain commended the organisers of the event for mobilising support for Atiku Abubakar, Ocho Obodoeze and other party candidates ahead of the 2027 elections. He, however, advised support groups not to rely solely on funding from the party or candidates but to mobilise resources from their members, stakeholders and supporters. Oji urged the groups to focus on grassroots mobilisation and communicate what he described as the party’s message of hope to Nigerians. He said citizens had the power to influence the direction of the country through their votes and called for greater participation in the democratic process. Among those present at the event were the Special Assistant to Atiku Abubakar on Special Duties, Dr. Ekene Onwuka; representative of the ADC presidential candidate’s wife, Anie Gift; ADC South-East Zonal Vice Chairman, Bon Unachukwu; and the Enugu State Caretaker Chairman, Gen. Chris Eze (rtd.). The post 2027: APC has failed Nigerians, ADC chieftain tells Tinubu, Mbah appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: PETROSOL secures approval to raise capital on Ghana Stock Exchange
items.description: PETROSOL Platinum Energy PLC, one of the leading oil marketing companies has received approval from the Ghana Stock Exchange and the Securities and Exchange Commission to raise long-term capital through the Ghana Stock Exchange, Managing Director Michael Bozumbil said. The approval marks a milestone for the company, which has evolved over two decades from a petroleum consulting firm into an indigenous oil marketing company in Ghana. “After a thorough assessment of PETROSOL’s business, including our governance systems, our compliance level, our credibility and growth plans, the Ghana Stock Exchange and the Securities and Exchange Commission have approved our request to raise patient capital on the stock exchange for our growth,” Bozumbil said at the Ghana International Petroleum Conference in Accra. He said the proceeds would fund the company’s long-term expansion strategy, including investments in renewable energy, solar power and electric vehicle charging infrastructure. “We have a clear plan to grow sustainably. We will continue to look for opportunities and the right partnerships to invest in the energy sector through innovation while taking advantage of government policies to expand our operations and deliver clean, long-lasting fuel and renewable energy solutions to our customers,” he said. Founded in 2006 as a petroleum business management and consulting firm, PETROSOL entered the oil marketing business in 2014, benefiting from government policies aimed at increasing indigenous participation in Ghana’s downstream petroleum sector. The company now operates more than 100 fuel stations across Ghana and employs about 490 people. Bozumbil attributed PETROSOL’s growth to corporate governance, prudent financial management and regulatory compliance despite challenging economic conditions. He said the company has obtained three International Organization for Standardization (ISO) certifications covering quality management, occupational health and safety, and environmental management. It has also received recognition from the Ghana Revenue Authority for tax compliance and remains in good standing with the National Petroleum Authority, the Environmental Protection Agency and the Ghana Standards Authority. Beyond its petroleum business, PETROSOL is investing in renewable energy and plans to install electric vehicle charging stations at selected service stations as part of Ghana’s energy transition. Bozumbil said policy consistency remains critical to enabling indigenous companies to compete with multinational firms in Ghana’s downstream petroleum sector. “As an indigenous company that has benefited from the consistent implementation of government policies promoting the growth of indigenous private companies, we believe collaboration and policy consistency are critical to building a resilient downstream petroleum industry,” he said. He said PETROSOL’s sponsorship of the 2026 Ghana International Petroleum Conference reflected its commitment to supporting industry dialogue and encouraging innovation, investment and sustainable growth. Looking ahead, Bozumbil said the company would continue expanding its retail fuel network, growing its renewable energy business and creating jobs. “We will continue to invest for growth. PETROSOL will remain a value-for-money brand, a good corporate citizen and an employer of choice. We will continue to energise dreams, ignite hope and power individuals and businesses to achieve their aspirations in an environmentally sustainable and ethical manner,” he said. The planned capital raise is expected to strengthen PETROSOL’s financial position and broaden investment opportunities in Ghana’s capital market, the company said.

items.title: Maison de l'Entreprise du Burkina Faso : Le premier Conseil d'administration officiellement installé
items.description: La Maison de l'Entreprise du Burkina Faso (MEBF) a officiellement installé son premier Conseil d'administration, ce vendredi 7 août 2026 à Ouagadougou. Cet évènement marque une nouvelle étape dans la mise en œuvre de sa réforme en tant qu'établissement public de l'État à caractère professionnel. Présidée par le directeur de Cabinet du ministre de l'Industrie, du commerce et de l'artisanat, Zakaria Gyengani, la cérémonie a également consacré l'installation du président du Conseil d'administration, Alassane Ouédraogo. Celui-ci a indiqué que cette réforme s'inscrit dans la vision de la Révolution progressiste populaire (RPP) et vise à faire de la MEBF une institution plus performante au service du développement entrepreneurial. Le nouveau Conseil d'administration entend notamment promouvoir la création et la structuration des entreprises, améliorer durablement l'environnement des affaires, accélérer la transformation digitale de l'institution et renforcer sa gouvernance. items.title: Osun Election: Reps minority caucus raises alarm over alleged intimidation
items.description: By Gift ChapiOdekina, Abuja The Minority Caucus of the House of Representatives has raised concerns over what it described as alleged intimidation of the Osun State Government ahead of next week’s governorship election. In a statement jointly signed on Friday by the Minority Leader, Hon. Fredrick Agbedi, and the Caucus Spokesman, Hon. Afam Victor Ogene, the lawmakers criticised President Bola Ahmed Tinubu’s directive to the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC) to vacate the order freezing the state’s accounts, describing it as an “afterthought.” The caucus argued that the President’s intervention came only after public criticism of the EFCC’s action, adding that it raised questions over the legality of the initial decision. The lawmakers cited comments attributed to EFCC spokesman Wilson Uwujaren that the accounts were frozen without a valid court order, noting that the President later directed the commission to approach the court to vacate the order. The caucus questioned the conflicting explanations surrounding the issue, asking whether a court order existed at the time the accounts were frozen and whether the President was fully aware of the actions of his appointees. The lawmakers also alleged a pattern of actions by the Federal Government that they claimed amounted to pressure on Osun State ahead of the election. They cited the alleged withholding of statutory allocations meant for local governments in the state, describing it as a move capable of affecting grassroots administration. The caucus further alleged that political violence involving some supporters of the All Progressives Congress (APC) and other groups had continued in the state, accusing security agencies of failing to respond adequately. It also criticised the arrest and detention of the Secretary to the Osun State Government, Teslim Igbalaiye, and others, describing the development as an attack on the state government’s institution. The lawmakers faulted the conduct of the Osun State Commissioner of Police and expressed concern over allegations made after the Inspector-General of Police’s visit to the state that the government was harbouring suspected criminals. “This is not policing. It is partisan propaganda in uniform,” the caucus said. The opposition lawmakers warned that the actions of some government officials could affect public confidence in the administration. “The mask is off. Nigerians can now see clearly that the APC has weaponised federal institutions against opposition states — a dress rehearsal of what is to come in the 2027 general elections,” the statement added. The caucus called on relevant stakeholders to ensure that Osun residents are allowed to exercise their voting rights freely and without intimidation. “The people of Osun should be given the enabling environment to freely exercise their constitutional right to vote, without fear, coercion or voter apathy,” it said. It urged civil society organisations and the international community to closely monitor developments before, during and after the election, while calling for accountability in the event of any breach of peace. “Osun people will vote. Osun people will be protected. And democracy will prevail,” the statement concluded. items.title: AI must empower entrepreneurs, not replace human creativity – UPS Global Director
items.description: Artificial intelligence (AI) should be viewed as a tool for strengthening entrepreneurship rather than replacing human creativity and critical thinking, Global Director of Social Impact at UPS, La’Kerri Jackson, has said. Speaking at the opening of a two-day entrepreneurship workshop in Accra on Thursday, Ms Jackson encouraged business owners to embrace AI as a practical tool for improving productivity while continuing to rely on their knowledge, experience and innovation. The workshop, organised by the International Trade Centre’s (ITC) SheTrades Initiative in partnership with UPS, Visa and the Ghana Export Promotion Authority (GEPA), has brought together 200 established and aspiring Ghanaian entrepreneurs. It is designed to build participants’ skills in artificial intelligence, digital payments, logistics, marketing and access to finance. According to Ms Jackson, entrepreneurs worldwide face similar challenges, particularly limited access to capital and export opportunities. She said this made collaboration between development partners and the private sector essential. “There are many challenges that entrepreneurs and small businesses face, from exporting challenges to the lack of access to capital. It’s not just specific to Ghana; it’s all over the globe,” she said. She noted that UPS works with organisations worldwide to help entrepreneurs overcome these barriers through training, mentorship and access to business support networks. Among the partnerships she highlighted were collaborations with Opportunity International to provide interest-free, collateral-free microloans; the Fearless Fund to support business growth; and the International Trade Centre to equip entrepreneurs with practical skills and resources. A key focus of the Accra workshop is helping small business owners understand how AI can be applied to their daily operations without requiring advanced technical expertise. Ms Jackson said many entrepreneurs already had access to free digital tools that could help improve their businesses. “It’s not as hard as we think it is. There are practical tools available through platforms like WhatsApp and Instagram for marketing, creating flyers and promoting businesses without investing a lot of money,” she said. She, however, cautioned entrepreneurs against becoming overly dependent on AI, stressing that technology should complement, rather than replace, human judgement. “The angle that people should take is that AI is a thought-leadership partner. You are the brands. You have the intellect. You have the intellectual property,” she said. “There is a danger in becoming so dependent on it, but everybody has to exercise discipline and continue to lean on their own intellect.” Also addressing participants, UPS Foundation Manager Bassen Anari challenged entrepreneurs to translate the lessons from the workshop into practical business actions. He observed that although many entrepreneurs enthusiastically participated in training programmes, only a few went on to implement what they had learnt.

items.title: Burkina: Les demandes d’agréments et de conventions au ministère de la Santé désormais sur « e-Agrément »
items.description: Burkina: Les demandes d’agréments et de conventions au ministère de la Santé désormais sur « e-Agrément » Ouagadougou, 7 août 2026 (AIB)- Le ministre de la Santé a officiellement lancé, vendredi à Ouagadougou, la plateforme « e-Agrément », destinée à simplifier et à accélérer les procédures de demande d’ouverture et d’exploitation des établissements privés de santé et les demandes de convention avec le ministère. Accessible à l’adresse https://e-agrement.minsante.bf/, la plateforme permet aux usagers de créer un compte, de choisir la procédure souhaitée, de renseigner le formulaire et de téléverser les pièces justificatives directement en ligne. Selon le directeur du Système d’information du ministère de la Santé, Dimitri Ouattara la plateforme est opérationnelle depuis fin avril 2026. Elle avait déjà enregistré, à la date du lancement officiel, 247 demandes, dont 39 ont abouti à une autorisation. « Avant, on avait une procédure en plus de 16 étapes », a-t-il expliqué, soulignant que la dématérialisation permet désormais aux usagers de suivre l’évolution de leurs dossiers en temps réel, sans avoir à effectuer de multiples déplacements. Le système permet également aux différents services habilités du ministère d’examiner les dossiers et de formuler leurs recommandations sur une même plateforme. Cette organisation devrait améliorer la traçabilité des dossiers et réduire les risques de perte de documents, tout en contribuant à raccourcir les délais de traitement, a ajouté le DSI. Le ministre de la Santé, Dr Robert Lucien Jean-Claude Kargougou, a présenté « e-Agrément » comme une première étape vers la création d’un « guichet unique de la santé » pour les procédures administratives qui seront progressivement dématérialisées. Il a rappelé qu’avant la mise en place de la plateforme, l’obtention d’une autorisation d’ouverture d’une formation sanitaire privée nécessitait 16 étapes et l’intervention de 11 intermédiaires. « Avec cette plateforme l’accès aux services devient beaucoup plus allégé, il y a beaucoup plus de transparence, beaucoup plus de simplification et beaucoup plus de traçabilité », a déclaré le ministre, invitant les professionnels de santé, les organisations de la société civile et les partenaires techniques et financiers à s’approprier la plateforme. La ministre en charge de la Transition digitale Aminata Zerbo/Sabane a, pour sa part, indiqué que ce lancement s’inscrit dans la dynamique gouvernementale d’accélération de la dématérialisation des services et procédures de l’administration publique. Elle a salué l’engagement du ministère de la Santé, qui mène également d’autres chantiers de transformation numérique, notamment la dématérialisation des licences d’affaires et la mise en place du système d’information hospitalier. « Ce sont des plateformes qui permettront en tout cas d’améliorer la qualité des services rendus à ces populations », a-t-elle affirmé, estimant que ces outils contribueront également à rendre l’administration sanitaire plus efficace. Parmi les premiers bénéficiaires de la plateforme figure l’ONG Jibayo, qui a obtenu une convention d’appui avec le ministère de la Santé. Son directeur pays, le Dr Jérémy Zoulana, a indiqué que la procédure, entamée en mai, a été finalisée en moins de trois mois. Il a expliqué que son organisation a pu créer son compte, renseigner les informations demandées et transmettre les pièces justificatives en ligne, tout en recevant régulièrement des informations sur l’état d’avancement du dossier. Selon lui, cette expérience contraste avec les procédures antérieures effectuées sur support papier, qui pouvaient prendre « autour d’une année », notamment en raison des risques de perte ou d’erreur dans les documents. Le Dr Zoulana a toutefois relevé que les difficultés rencontrées étaient principalement liées à la connexion internet et non au fonctionnement de la plateforme, ajoutant que son organisation a bénéficié d’une assistance des responsables du ministère tout au long de la procédure. À travers « e-Agrément », le ministère de la Santé entend ainsi poursuivre la modernisation de ses procédures administratives et faciliter l’accès des usagers à ses services. Agence d’information du Burkina YOS/ata

items.title: Osun Election: Police deploy four officers per polling unit — IGP
items.description: ….Names of senior officers to be withheld until election day …IGP assures voters of adequate protection, warns politicians against violence By Kingsley Omonobi Ahead of the Osun State governorship election, the Inspector-General of Police (IGP), Olatunji Disu, has announced the deployment of a minimum of four police officers to each of the over 3,000 polling units across the state to ensure a safe and credible electoral process. Disu disclosed this during a stakeholder engagement with civil society organisations on election security, where he assured residents of adequate police protection before, during and after the election. The IGP, however, raised concerns over alleged attempts by some politicians to identify senior police officers assigned to specific local government areas ahead of the election. He said although he had approved the deployment list comprising Assistant Inspectors-General of Police (AIGs), Commissioners of Police (CPs) and other senior officers, the details would not be released until the election day. “We have noticed politicians making frantic efforts to identify the senior officers that will be deployed to each local government area for reasons best known to them. Even though I have approved the list of senior officers to be deployed, it will not be released until the day of the election to ensure a free, fair and credible exercise,” Disu said. The police chief urged residents of Osun State to come out en masse to vote, assuring them that the Nigeria Police Force had put in place a robust security arrangement to protect voters, electoral officials and other stakeholders. The assurance came amid concerns over political violence in parts of the state, with civil society groups identifying 13 local government areas as high-risk areas and linking about 34 fatalities to violence as of June. Disu said the police were aware of security challenges in the state, including cult-related activities, which he said had been exploited by some political actors. “We have issues of cultism in Osun already. It became easier for different parties to attack each other using the existing animosity in the state,” he said. He explained that the police had intervened when violence escalated, leading to the decision for the Commissioner of Police in the state to step aside while another officer oversees election security arrangements. He added that an Assistant Inspector-General of Police would soon be deployed to Osun to strengthen the security architecture for the election. The IGP described the Osun governorship election, which is the last off-cycle election before the 2027 general elections, as a significant test for the Nigeria Police Force and the country. “Officers know the implications of going contrary to their assigned duties and roles on election day. No election or political contest is worth losing any life, as elections will come and go,” he said. Disu appealed to political parties, candidates and their supporters to conduct themselves peacefully before, during and after the election. He also warned police personnel deployed for the election against allowing themselves to be used for unlawful activities. “I have warned my men not to allow themselves to be used as cannon fodder. You have families and you have a name. Do not soil that name because of an election that will come and go,” he said. The IGP also warned politicians against deploying thugs, saying the absence of violence would contribute significantly to a peaceful electoral process. “Let the elections go freely. Do not deploy thugs. If they do not deploy thugs, there will be no problems with the election. But we will ensure security, free and fair election,” he said. Earlier, Executive Director of Yiaga Africa, Samson Itodo, described the Osun governorship election as a “litmus test” for rebuilding public trust and confidence in Nigeria’s electoral process. Itodo expressed concerns over the security situation in the state, noting that 13 local government areas had been identified as high-risk areas due to recurring violence and killings. He urged security agencies, particularly the police, to remain neutral and resist attempts by political actors to compromise the election. He listed Osogbo, Irewole, Ifedayo and Ife North among local government areas classified as critical-risk zones, while Boripe, Ife Central and Ife East were identified as areas requiring heightened security attention. Itodo stressed that the conduct of security agencies would play a major role in determining voters’ confidence in the electoral process. He urged security personnel to ensure fairness, protect all stakeholders and avoid actions capable of undermining the credibility of the election. items.description: Real Madrid’s Argentine playmaker Franco Mastantuono has joined Fiorentina on loan, the Serie A outfit announced on Friday. The 18-year-old will spend one season in Italy under the current agreement, according to a brief announcement on Real’s website. Mastantuono signed at the Bernabeu last summer after catching the eye in his homeland with River Plate and becoming, aged 17 years and nine months, the youngest player to represent the Argentina national team in an official match. He moved to Spain on a six-year deal after Real shelled out just over 63 million euros ($72 million) to secure his services. The teenager made 35 appearances across all competitions last season for Los Blancos, scoring three goals, but failed to nail down a starting spot as he missed out on Argentina’s World Cup squad. items.title: Bobo-Dioulasso : Le ministre Yacouba Zabré Gouba met en service la centrale thermique Bobo 2 de 26,4 MW
items.description: Le Burkina Faso renforce davantage sa capacité nationale de production d’électricité. La nouvelle centrale thermique Bobo 2, d’une puissance de 26,4 MW, a été officiellement mise en service ce vendredi 7 août 2026 à Bobo-Dioulasso, par le ministre de l’Énergie, des Mines et des Carrières, Yacouba Zabré Gouba. C'était en présence de plusieurs autorités administratives, coutumières, religieuses, militaires et paramilitaires. La mise en service de cette centrale s’inscrit dans la dynamique engagée par le Gouvernement pour accroître les capacités nationales de production d’électricité et réduire la dépendance énergétique du Burkina Faso vis-à-vis de l’extérieur. La plaque d'inauguration Selon le Directeur général de la Société nationale d’électricité du Burkina (SONABEL), Souleymane Ouédraogo, la centrale Bobo 2 est constituée de trois groupes électrogènes équipés de moteurs MAN, d’une puissance unitaire de 8,8 MW, portant la capacité totale de l’infrastructure à 26,4 MW. L’installation comprend également des équipements de stockage de combustible, un système d’évacuation de l’énergie composé de trois transformateurs de 12 MVA, ainsi que plusieurs dispositifs auxiliaires destinés à assurer la fiabilité et la sécurité de son exploitation. L'intérieur de la centrale… Un investissement de plus de 33 milliards de francs CFA Entièrement financé sur fonds propres de la SONABEL, le projet a nécessité un investissement de 33,893 milliards de FCFA TTC. Sa réalisation a été confiée à l’entreprise PPI Burkina et s’est achevée en 15 mois, un délai jugé particulièrement satisfaisant au regard de la complexité technique de l’ouvrage. « Cette réalisation a été un véritable défi logistique, technique et technologique », a relevé le Directeur général de la SONABEL, saluant le professionnalisme et l’engagement des équipes ayant contribué à la réalisation de la centrale. Le ministre Yacouba Zabré Gouba montrant sa joie de voie cette infrastructure énergie être en marche Avec cet apport de 26,4 MW, la puissance installée du site de Bobo-Dioulasso passe de 60 MW à 86,4 MW, renforçant ainsi significativement l’offre énergétique disponible dans la région du Guiriko. Une énergie destinée à l’ensemble du Burkina Pour le ministre Yacouba Zabré Gouba, cette infrastructure ne bénéficiera pas uniquement à Bobo-Dioulasso ou à la région du Guiriko. Grâce au Réseau national interconnecté, l’énergie produite pourra être injectée dans le réseau national et contribuer à l’alimentation de différentes localités du pays. Le site de la centrale thermique Le ministre Gouba a souligné que cette centrale permettra notamment de soutenir les unités industrielles et économiques, d’améliorer la qualité du service public d’électricité et de contribuer à l’amélioration des conditions de vie des populations. Une dynamique qui se poursuit La centrale Bobo 2 constitue l’une des quatre infrastructures énergétiques engagées dans le cadre des projets d’urgence du Gouvernement. Après la mise en service des installations de Pabré, la dynamique se poursuivra avec les centrales thermiques de Koudougou (25 MW) et de Kaya (25 MW), dont les inaugurations sont respectivement prévues les 10 et 11 août 2026. Une vue des groupes de la centrale À terme, le Gouvernement ambitionne d’étendre ces investissements à d’autres régions, notamment Ouahigouya, Banfora et Gaoua, afin de renforcer l’autonomisation stratégique du Burkina Faso et de faire de la souveraineté énergétique un levier de l’industrialisation et de la transformation économique nationale. items.title: Navy recovers 105,000 litres of suspected stolen crude, uncovers illegal storage facilities in Delta
items.description: By Kingsley Omonobi The Nigerian Navy has recovered about 105,000 litres of products suspected to be stolen crude oil during a series of anti-crude oil theft operations in Delta State. The operations, conducted under Operation Delta Sentinel within the Nigerian Navy Ship (NNS) Delta Area of Operation, also led to the discovery of concealed storage facilities allegedly used by suspected oil thieves to stockpile stolen crude. Director of Naval Information, Navy Captain Abiodun Folorunsho, said the recovered products comprised approximately 60,000 litres and 45,000 litres found at separate locations in the Oteghele axis of Delta State. According to him, the recoveries highlight both the persistence of crude oil theft and the Navy’s determination to dismantle the infrastructure supporting the illegal trade. “The operations form part of sustained efforts to disrupt crude oil theft networks, protect critical oil and gas assets, and prevent economic losses to the nation,” Folorunsho said. He added that the latest operation underscores the effectiveness of the Navy’s ongoing offensive against crude oil theft and illegal bunkering across the Niger Delta. According to the Navy spokesman, the success recorded under Operation Delta Sentinel reflects sustained efforts to degrade criminal networks involved in economic sabotage and protect the country’s oil and gas infrastructure. Folorunsho reaffirmed the Nigerian Navy’s commitment to safeguarding Nigeria’s maritime environment through continuous operations aimed at combating crude oil theft, enhancing national security and supporting the nation’s economic development. The post Navy recovers 105,000 litres of suspected stolen crude, uncovers illegal storage facilities in Delta appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Tinubu welcomes Nigeria into World Energy Council
items.description: By Johnbosco Agbakwuru, Abuja President Bola Tinubu, has welcomed the formal admission of Nigeria as the newest National Member Committee of the World Energy Council (WEC), describing it as a proud moment for the nation and a strong vote of confidence in Nigeria’s energy reforms and leadership role in Africa. The President said Nigeria’s entry into the century-old global network of over 100 countries positions the country to more actively shape global discourse on energy security, equity and sustainability. President Tinubu congratulated the inaugural leadership of WEC Nigeria – Mr Abdulrazaq Isa, OFR, as Chairman and Mr Bala Wunti as Chief Executive Officer – alongside other distinguished Nigerians drawn from across the energy value chain, regulatory institutions, industry associations, finance, academia and the Future Energy Leaders community, who will serve as inaugural Board members. He described Mr Isa as a distinguished patriot and trailblazing industrialist whose pioneering investments in indigenous refining and industrial energy have opened a new frontier for Nigerian enterprise. The President described Mr Wunti as one of Nigeria’s finest energy strategists and reform champions whose over three decades of exemplary service, defined by integrity and strategic vision, have been marked by landmark reforms that significantly enhanced national revenues and restored investor confidence in Nigeria’s energy sector. He said the blend of seasoned industry captains, regulators, finance experts and youth leaders on the Board gives WEC Nigeria the balance, neutrality and credibility required to succeed. According to him: “Nigeria has joined the World Energy Council to lead, not just participate – to ensure Africa’s voice shapes global energy decisions.” The President affirmed the full support of the Federal Government for WEC Nigeria as a neutral, technology-agnostic platform for policy dialogue, investment mobilisation and innovation, and reiterated Nigeria’s commitment to work with WEC London and its global community to deliver secure, affordable and sustainable energy for all. He wished the Chairman, CEO and the inaugural Board every success in this historic national assignment. The post Tinubu welcomes Nigeria into World Energy Council appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: 2027: Benue residents promise massive vote for Tinubu over infrastructure drive
items.description: …— As presidential media team inspects federal, state projects By Johnbosco Agbakwuru, Abuja Jubilant Benue residents on Thursday promised to vote massively for President Bola Tinubu in the 2027 elections to show appreciation for his infrastructural drive, especially the expansion of connectivity through strategic road and bridge projects. This came as the Presidential Media Team, in collaboration with the Renewed Hope Ambassadors, inspected key federal and Benue State government infrastructure projects across the state. The inspection covered the ongoing Buruku-Logo Bridge, the Wurukum Overhead Bridge in Makurdi, the 22-kilometre Makurdi–Gboko Road, and major state projects, including the completed High-Level Roundabout Interchange in Makurdi and the Gboko underpass and interchange. The Makurdi–Gboko Road forms part of Phase II of the Abuja–Keffi–Akwanga–Lafia–Makurdi Expressway, a strategic corridor linking North Central Nigeria with the South-East. It is expected to be completed by December 2027. The Renewed Hope Ambassadors’ national media tour, which includes over 40 editors and journalists, is designed to independently assess, document and showcase the implementation and impact of key federal and state government projects under President Tinubu’s administration. The delegation was led by the Special Adviser to the President on Information and Strategy, Mr. Bayo Onanuga. Speaking during the inspection, Onanuga said the Buruku-Logo Bridge is one of five federal government bridges under construction in Benue State and demonstrates the administration’s commitment to investing borrowed funds in productive infrastructure. He said the project would reconnect previously isolated communities, reduce travel time, improve access to markets for farmers and strengthen economic integration across Benue, Taraba and Adamawa states. According to him, the projects are being financed through the Renewed Hope Infrastructure Development Fund, and he assured that funding remains adequate for timely completion. Onanuga, in a statement by Tunde Rahman, Director of Media and Publicity, RHA, was quoted as saying: “This bridge in particular is the fifth bridge the federal government is building in Benue State. I think as Nigerians you see that the government has been accused of so many things, including taking loans. “You can now see where the money is going. It is to develop infrastructure, to link people who have been forgotten before, to make sure that at least commerce flows freely. “Farmers can get their products straight to the market, and they can shorten the travel time between one community and another, especially between the rural areas and the capital. “You can see that this one where we are now, the one in Buruku, is going to affect three states — Taraba, Adamawa and Benue — and of course it means benefits for Nigeria.” The team also inspected the ongoing 25.6-kilometre Captain Dan Road from Lubona Junction to the Tor Tiv Palace, the Food Basket Brewery Limited in Makurdi, and the federal government-funded rehabilitation of the Buruku–Gboko Water Treatment Plant at Ameladu Headworks, one of the state’s largest water infrastructure projects. A major highlight of the tour was the inspection of the 1,754-metre Buruku-Logo Bridge. The project links agrarian communities across the River Benue, provides access to neighbouring Taraba State and is expected to boost agriculture, commerce and regional integration. The contractor also employs more than 50 workers from the host community. Residents expressed appreciation to President Tinubu for prioritising infrastructure that addresses longstanding transportation challenges. They described the bridge as a life-saving intervention that would end years of dangerous river crossings and improve the livelihoods of surrounding communities. They also expect the bridge, on completion, to eliminate frequent boat accidents experienced during the rainy season while creating employment opportunities for local youths engaged on the project. Many residents also pledged continued support for President Tinubu’s Renewed Hope agenda, saying the visible impact of ongoing projects had renewed public confidence in the federal government. Speaking with journalists, the Deputy Governor of Benue State, Dr. Samuel Ode, said the state remained grateful for the federal government’s infrastructure investments and expressed confidence that the people would strongly support President Tinubu’s re-election in 2027. He described the ongoing Wurukum Overhead Bridge as a critical intervention on the Abuja–Lafia–Makurdi–Enugu corridor, noting that the junction had for years been notorious for severe traffic congestion, particularly during festive periods. According to him, President Tinubu approved the project following a request by Governor Hyacinth Alia, and construction is progressing rapidly. The Deputy Governor also highlighted the state government’s investment in the Makurdi Central Interchange and underpass, describing it as a transformative project that connects key routes linking Government House, the central business district, Wurukum and the Abuja–Enugu highway, while significantly improving traffic flow within the state capital. “Actually, this road serves as the gateway between the north of the country and the south. Before now we used to have heavy gridlock here, especially during festivities, so the governor of Benue State approached Mr. President for us to have an overhead bridge here. “The President, in his magnanimity, graciously approved the construction of this overhead bridge. So work has commenced, moving at a very high speed, and the people of Benue are happy because we used to experience quite a lot of difficulties at this point.” The post 2027: Benue residents promise massive vote for Tinubu over infrastructure drive appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Liberté d’expression en France : «le moindre avis alternatif est dans le collimateur», dénonce la diplomatie russe
items.description: « Nous considerons inacceptables et condamnons fermement la persecution politique des journalistes sur la base d'accusations sans fondement », a declare le 6 août, lors d'un point presse , Alexeï Fadeïev, porte-parole adjoint de la diplomatie russe. Celui-ci est revenu sur le recent arrete d'expulsion pris a l'encontre de Xenia Fedorova, qui dirigeait la branche francaise de RT et qui etait devenue chroniqueuse sur CNews. Un poste d'ou elle abordait notamment le conflit en Ukraine, evoquant la perception russe de ce dernier. Une demarche, relevant de la deontologie journalistique, qui lui a valu d'etre qualifiee de « relais du Kremlin » par ses detracteurs. Ces derniers furent d'ailleurs nombreux a se rejouir publiquement de l'arrete d'expulsion visant Xenia Fedorova, puis du gel de ses avoirs decide par des autorites francaises qui ont pris fait et cause pour Kiev . « L'expulsion de Xenia Fedorova, en tant qu'acte de represailles contre une journaliste "recalcitrante", ne nous a pas surpris », a ajoute Alexeï Fadeïev. « Nous constatons depuis longtemps que les autorites francaises associent systematiquement tout probleme dans le pays a une "trace russe" », a-t-il poursuivi, alors que plusieurs pretendants a la fonction supreme en France – et pas les mieux places dans les intentions de vote – pretendent depuis plusieurs jours etre la cible d'une operation russe. Classement RSF sur la liberte de la presse : la place de la France « manifestement surevaluee » « Tout point de vue alternatif est qualifie de "propagande des narratifs russes" et s'accompagne de tentatives de museler le journaliste ou le media concerne de l'espace informationnel », a encore declare Fadeïev. « Il s'agit d'une lutte qui s'intensifie et qui prend de plus en plus souvent la forme de mesures punitives prises a l'encontre de medias et de journalistes juges indesirables », a-t-il ajoute, lui qui a notamment rappele le sort qui fut celui de RT France et Sputnik apres l'eclatement du conflit en Ukraine. « La liberte de la presse et la liberte de l'expression, si bruyamment proclamees en paroles, sont en realite cyniquement bafouees, des qu'une position diverge du "courant dominant" neoliberal ou antirusse », a assene le diplomate. « Il serait toutefois incorrect d'affirmer que les autorites du pays s'en prennent uniquement aux medias russes. Le moindre avis alternatif est dans le collimateur », a-t-il poursuivi, avant de conclure : « Il est revelateur que la France n'est plus consideree, meme parmi ses partenaires, comme un bastion de la veritable liberte de la presse : dans le classement de l'ONG Reporters sans frontieres, notoirement partiale, elle appartient meme a la categorie "satisfaisante" et occupe la 25e place, manifestement surevaluee. »

items.title: APC challenges court judgment, files stay of execution in Owo/Ose ticket tussle
items.description: —As INEC retains Adelegbe as party candidate By Dayo Johnson Akure The Independent National Electoral Commission, INEC, has retained Hon. Timehin Adelegbe as the All Progressives Congress, APC, candidate for the Owo/Ose Federal Constituency pending the determination of an appeal. Its decision follows the APC’s filing of a Notice of Appeal and a Motion for Stay of Execution against the judgment of the Federal High Court, Abuja, which declared another aspirant, Abdulghani Rotimi Arobo, as the party’s candidate. In a letter dated August 6, 2026, addressed to the INEC Chairman and signed by A.G. Yirvoms Ayuba of Sozo Attorneys, the party notified the commission of the appeal. “We wish to formally notify the Commission that the 1st Defendant has today, the 6th day of August, 2026, filed a Notice of Appeal at the Registry of the Federal High Court, Abuja, expressing its dissatisfaction with the judgment delivered by Hon. Justice Peter O. Lifu on the 5th of August, 2026,” the letter read. “Furthermore, please be informed that we have also filed a Motion for Stay of Execution of the said judgment pending the hearing and determination of the appeal.” The party urged INEC to “stay all actions regarding the enforcement of the orders contained in the judgment” and “maintain the status quo until the judicial processes now pending before the Court are resolved.” Copies of the Notice of Appeal and Motion for Stay of Execution were attached to the letter. The Ondo State Electoral Commissioner was also notified. A reliable party source in the APC Secretariat said that INEC had continued to recognise Adelegbe as the candidate pending the appeal. “As things stand, Hon. Timehin Adelegbe remains the candidate recognised by the commission pending the final determination of the appeal,” the source said. The source added that the APC had commenced an internal investigation into the result relied upon by the Federal High Court in declaring Arobo the winner. “The party is investigating the result the plaintiff claimed showed he scored 7,959 votes in Owo Local Government Area and 2,583 votes in Ose Local Government Area. ” There are questions over how the result sheet was obtained and the circumstances surrounding its emergence,” the source said. The party is also reviewing whether the document presented in court emanated from its official records. Justice Peter Lifu of the Federal High Court, Abuja, had on August 5 declared Arobo as the APC candidate for Owo/Ose after holding that he won the party’s primary election. The APC has since challenged the judgment at the Court of Appeal, expressing confidence that the appellate court will resolve the legal and factual issues in dispute. items.title: Appui aux Pme sénégalaises : l’Adepme et la Jica consolident leur coopération
items.description: Faire de l’amélioration continue et du renforcement des capacités des entreprises des leviers durables de transformation et de compétitivité du tissu économique sénégalais, c’est ce que visent l’Agence de Développement et d’Encadrement des Petites et Moyennes Entreprises (Adepme) et la Jica dans le cadre de leur coopération. L’Agence de Développement et d’Encadrement des Petites et Moyennes Entreprises (Adepme) a reçu une délégation de la Jica (Japan International Cooperation Agency), conduite par Ogata Erina, première adjointe à la Représentante Résidente, dans le cadre d’une séance de travail consacrée au renforcement de la coopération entre les deux institutions. Cette coopération entre l’Adepme et la Jica traduit, selon une note de l’Adepme rendue publique vendredi, une ambition partagée : celle de faire de l’amélioration continue et du renforcement des capacités des entreprises des leviers durables de transformation et de compétitivité du tissu économique sénégalais. A lire aussi : Financement et d’accompagnement des PME : Adepme et la BERD lancent une nouvelle dynamique « Les échanges ont notamment porté sur l’état d’avancement de la demande d’affectation d’un Expert Kaizen auprès de l’Adepme, ainsi que sur les perspectives de collaboration autour de cette approche, reconnue comme un levier d’amélioration continue, de productivité et de compétitivité des entreprises », renseigne le texte. À cette occasion, poursuit la même source, le Directeur général de l’Adepme, Ismaïla Kébé a salué la qualité du partenariat avec la JICA et souligné l’intérêt de poursuivre cette coopération afin de renforcer les dispositifs d’accompagnement destinés aux PME sénégalaises. Mariama DIEME

items.title: Ghana: Genser energy buys back Oppenheimer partners’ stake as investor exits after five years
items.description: Genser Energy has bought back the entire stake held by Oppenheimer Partners, completing the investment firm’s exit after five years and marking a new phase in the Ghanaian energy company’s regional expansion. The privately owned energy infrastructure company said it had redeemed the full shareholding previously held by OP Energy Holdings Limited, ending Oppenheimer Partners’ investment in the business. Oppenheimer Partners first invested in Genser Energy as a preferred shareholder in 2021 before converting its holding into common equity in 2023, when it acquired a 40.4% stake. The latest transaction concludes that investment and returns the shares to Genser Energy. Founded in 2006, Genser Energy has grown into one of West Africa’s integrated energy companies, supplying electricity to industrial customers and utilities while investing in natural gas infrastructure. Before Oppenheimer Partners’ investment, the company had developed five operating power plants and a 325-km natural gas pipeline network, becoming a key supplier of energy to Ghana’s industrial sector. During the investment period, Genser expanded its infrastructure by adding about 110 km of natural gas pipeline, constructing a 200 million standard cubic feet per day gas conditioning plant in Prestea and entering Côte d’Ivoire through cross-border electricity exports. “This transaction marks an important milestone for Genser Energy and reflects the strength of the business we have built over the past two decades,” Baafour Asiamah Adjei, the company’s founder, president and chief executive, said. Chairman Nana Osae Nyampong said the buyback would enable the company to focus on its next phase of growth. “As we look ahead, we remain focused on expanding our regional presence and creating long-term value for our customers, communities, employees and shareholders,” Nyampong said. The transaction comes as infrastructure investors increasingly target Africa’s energy sector, where rising industrial demand and regional power integration are driving investment in gas pipelines, power generation and cross-border electricity trade. Genser said it remains positioned for further expansion through continued investment in strategic energy infrastructure across West Africa. The company operates more than 310 megawatts of installed generation capacity and owns a 436-km privately developed natural gas pipeline network in Ghana. It is also completing major midstream projects, including a gas conditioning plant and a natural gas liquids export terminal, while supplying power to industrial customers and utilities and participating in regional electricity exports.

items.title: Kick-boxing : la Marocaine Amber Tsoudali sacrée championne de l'ISKA China Open 2026
items.description: La jeune prodige marocaine Amber Tsoudali a remporté le titre de l'ISKA China Open & World Elite Invitational 2026, disputé à Sanya, en Chine, en s'imposant en finale face à la Chinoise Shi Yan Yan. Âgée de seulement 14 ans, la championne marocaine s'est imposée aux points (90-82) au terme de trois reprises, décrochant ainsi la médaille d'or dans sa catégorie et ajoutant un nouveau titre international à son palmarès. La cérémonie officielle de remise des récompenses est prévue dimanche à Sanya, où Amber Tsoudali recevra son trophée de championne de l'ISKA China Open 2026. À l'issue de son sacre, la jeune athlète, qui représente le Maroc et la Belgique, a reconnu que cette finale n'avait pas été son meilleur combat. « Ce n'était pas mon meilleur combat, mais j'ai montré que j'étais capable de rester concentrée et de trouver des solutions dans les moments difficiles », a-t-elle confié à Hesport. Amber Tsoudali a expliqué que la compétition s'était déroulée dans des conditions particulières, marquées par des changements de programme de dernière minute, une longue attente avant son combat et une communication tardive concernant l'horaire de la finale. Malgré ces difficultés, elle est parvenue à conserver sa concentration jusqu'au bout. La jeune championne s'est dite heureuse de décrocher cette médaille d'or, tout en affirmant vouloir continuer à progresser. « Je suis heureuse de remporter cette médaille d'or, mais je sais que je peux faire encore mieux. Cette victoire me motive à continuer de travailler et à m'entraîner encore davantage » , a-t-elle déclaré. Après ce succès en Chine, Amber Tsoudali enchaînera avec un calendrier particulièrement chargé. Elle participera le 8 octobre à une compétition ISKA en Espagne, avant de prendre part à un tournoi en Allemagne le 10 octobre, puis au championnat WBC en Italie le 15 octobre. Elle clôturera sa saison internationale avec le Championnat de Belgique, prévu le 19 octobre. À seulement 14 ans, Amber Tsoudali confirme ainsi son immense potentiel et s'impose comme l'un des grands espoirs marocains du kick-boxing sur la scène internationale. The post Kick-boxing : la Marocaine Amber Tsoudali sacrée championne de l'ISKA China Open 2026 appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Hommage à feu Agokoli IV : Les festivités d’Agbogboza 2026 annulées, seule la cérémonie rituelle est maintenue
items.description: Lomé, 7 août (ATOP) – L’Union Eweto a annoncé l’annulation des activités festives de l’édition 2026 de la fête traditionnelle Agbogboza. Cette décision est liée au décès de Ewefiaga Togbuï Dzidzor Kossi Fafagbé Agboli Agokoli IV, président du Conseil national des chefs traditionnels du Togo et président du Bureau exécutif de l’Union Eweto. Dans un communiqué publié le 5 août, l’Union Eweto indique que seule la cérémonie rituelle sera organisée cette année. Elle se déroulera le jeudi 3 septembre au sanctuaire Agbogbodzi. Les dignitaires et les prêtres sacrificateurs seront chargés d’accomplir les rites traditionnels. Cette décision fait suite au décès de Togbuï Agokoli IV, chef du canton de Notsé et roi du peuple Ewe du Togo, du Ghana, du Bénin, du Nigéria et de la diaspora. Il est décédé le 1er février 2026. Considéré comme un gardien des traditions, de l’histoire et de l’identité du peuple Ewe, il était une figure importante de la chefferie traditionnelle. L’Union Eweto invite les populations à se retrouver en 2027 pour la prochaine édition de la fête traditionnelle Agbogboza. ATOP/La Rédaction

items.title: Factbox-What is the Patriot missile system and why are supplies depleted worldwide?
items.description: WASHINGTON, Aug 7 (Reuters) - First used in the 1991 Gulf War, the U.S. Patriot air defense system has seen demand spike sharply this year, with supplies of interceptor missiles depleted by Ukraine's war against the Russian invasion and the widening war in the Middle East. Ukraine is urgently seeking more Patriot interceptors to defend against a nightly barrage of Russian ballistic missile strikes. But the Iran war has drained arsenals in the U.S. and the Gulf, and some European countries are holding onto missiles they may need for their own defense.

items.title: Okowa backs state police, says reform will strengthen fight against insecurity
items.description: By Ochuko Akuopha, Asaba Immediate past Governor of Delta State, Senator Ifeanyi Okowa, has described President Bola Tinubu’s push for the establishment of state police as a bold step towards addressing Nigeria’s security challenges and deepening the devolution of powers to the states. Okowa said the campaign for state police dates back to 2000, noting that previous administrations had been reluctant to pursue the reform. “The agitation for state police started as far back as the year 2000. No president had been bold enough to allow the devolution of power. But this president is bold enough to say that this is the best way to ensure that we are able to secure the land,” he said. Speaking on Friday at the All Progressives Congress (APC) Delta North Stakeholders’ Meeting in Asaba, Okowa argued that state police would better position governors to tackle insecurity in their respective states. The meeting also endorsed President Tinubu and Delta State Governor Sheriff Oborevwori for second terms in the 2027 general elections. The motion for the endorsement was moved by the APC House of Representatives candidate for Aniocha/Oshimili Federal Constituency, Mr. Ndudi Elumelu, and seconded by Mr. Frank Esenwa. It was unanimously adopted by stakeholders. Okowa stressed that the proposed state police system would complement, rather than replace, the Nigeria Police Force. “We are not talking about ending the federal police. Let each state have its own police, committed to its people, properly trained, properly armed and dedicated to securing the land,” he said. According to the former governor, Nigeria requires leaders who are prepared to take difficult decisions in the national interest. “We want a president who is able to take bold decisions that will secure today and the future. The lives of Nigerians matter more than what is politically correct,” he added. Also speaking, Delta State Deputy Governor, Sir Monday Onyeme, called for unity and cohesion within the APC ahead of the 2027 elections. He urged party members to reconcile with aggrieved aspirants who lost out during the party’s primaries and encourage them to work for the party’s success. Onyeme also commended President Tinubu for supporting the state police initiative. “We need state police because the federal police cannot reach all the nooks and crannies. Today, it is becoming a reality. Who made that possible? President Bola Ahmed Tinubu,” he said. The Delta State APC Chairman, Chief Solomon Areyenka, and the party’s Delta North Chairman, Mr. Dan Ossai, also urged members to remain united and work diligently to ensure the party’s success in the 2027 general elections. items.title: Propos du Président nigérian sur la situation sécuritaire dans l’AES : le Burkina Faso, le Mali et le Niger expriment leur profond regret
items.description: Le Ministre des Affaires étrangères, le Camarade Karamoko Jean Marie TRAORÉ, a reçu, dans la soirée du jeudi 06 août 2026, le Chargé d’Affaires de l’Ambassade de la République fédérale du Nigéria au Burkina Faso, à la suite des déclarations du Président nigérian, Bola Ahmed TINUBU, sur la situation sécuritaire dans les pays de la Confédération des États du Sahel (AES). Cette rencontre s’est déroulée en présence des Chargés d’Affaires des Ambassades du Mali et du Niger, illustrant la position concertée et solidaire des trois États membres de la Confédération. Le 30 juillet dernier, lors d’une rencontre avec des chefs traditionnels nigérians, le Président TINUBU a imputé la recrudescence des enlèvements et des attaques terroristes au Nigéria à ce qu’il a qualifié d’« effondrement » de la sécurité dans les pays voisins du Sahel. « Certains d’entre eux (les terroristes) ne sont pas Nigérians. Vous voyez, le problème de l’insécurité au Mali, au Burkina Faso et au Niger ne fait qu’aggraver nos difficultés. », avait affirmé le Président TINUBU devant les chefs traditionnels nigérians. Au nom de ses homologues du Mali et du Niger, le Ministre Karamoko Jean Marie TRAORÉ a exprimé le profond regret des pays de la Confédération face à ces propos inexacts et peu compatibles avec l’esprit de solidarité qui doit prévaloir entre États voisins confrontés à une menace commune. Selon le Chef de la diplomatie burkinabè, cette lecture de la situation sécuritaire occulte les sacrifices considérables consentis quotidiennement par les Forces de défense et de sécurité, ainsi que par les populations, du Burkina Faso, du Mali et du Niger dans la lutte contre le terrorisme. « C’est une analyse rapide, très simpliste et surprenante, qui révèle un biais préoccupant de la part de la première autorité du Nigéria. Nous aurions souhaité que le contexte sécuritaire soit présenté avec davantage de justesse, plutôt que de faire porter à des pays voisins la responsabilité d’une situation complexe, au risque d’alimenter des incompréhensions et des frustrations entre des peuples liés par l’histoire, la géographie et la fraternité », a déclaré le Ministre TRAORÉ. Pour le cas particulier du Niger, le ministre des Affaires étrangères estime que les propos du Président TINUBU constituent un mépris du sacrifice consenti par l’armée nigérienne face à Boko Haram depuis des années, alors que le phénomène de terrorisme ne sévissait pas encore dans les pays de la Confédération AES. Le Ministre a par ailleurs rappelé que malgré les connexions établies entre Boko Haram et certains groupes terroristes actifs au Sahel, les États de la Confédération AES se sont toujours gardés de toute accusation publique contre le Nigéria, privilégiant une approche fondée sur la coopération et la responsabilité partagée. Pour le Chef de la diplomatie burkinabè, « le Burkina Faso, le Mali, le Niger et le Nigéria font face au même ennemi. À ce titre, les succès enregistrés par les Forces de défense et de sécurité des pays de l’AES bénéficient à la sécurité de l’ensemble de la sous-région, y compris du Nigéria, en limitant les capacités de nuisance et la mobilité des groupes terroristes ». Le Ministre TRAORÉ a ainsi invité les autorités nigérianes à privilégier des discours fédérateurs et porteurs de solidarité, plutôt que des déclarations susceptibles d’alimenter les divisions ou les malentendus entre peuples voisins. « Nous ne sommes pas responsables de ce qui nous arrive. Nous en payons la facture, mais les véritables ennemis sont ailleurs. C’est pourquoi nous devons agir comme des peuples frères, unis par une même histoire et confrontés à une même menace », a-t-il souligné. Le Ministre Karamoko Jean Marie TRAORÉ a réaffirmé que la démarche des trois pays de la Confédération AES ne relevait ni de la polémique ni de la confrontation diplomatique, mais traduisait la volonté d’entretenir un dialogue franc, respectueux et constructif entre États frères, convaincus que seule une coopération sincère permettra de relever durablement les défis sécuritaires de la sous-région. En réponse, le Chargé d’Affaires de l’Ambassade du Nigéria a indiqué avoir pris bonne note du message qui lui a été transmis et s’est engagé à en rendre fidèlement compte à ses autorités à Abuja. Il a, par ailleurs, reconnu les efforts considérables consentis par les pays de la Confédération des États du Sahel dans la lutte contre le terrorisme, citant notamment le rôle déterminant joué par le Niger dans la prévention d’attaques qui auraient pu viser le territoire nigérian. Le diplomate nigérian a enfin salué la démarche des Ministres des Affaires étrangères de la Confédération AES, y voyant la volonté des États voisins de privilégier le dialogue, la compréhension mutuelle et la solidarité face à une menace commune. DCRP/MAE

JI protests cause traffic disruptions across Karachi
items.description: Several major thoroughfares in Karachi were blocked or affected by traffic disruptions on Friday as Jamaat-i-Islami held protest sit-ins in the city as part of a nationwide demonstration against the petroleum levy. A day earlier, the party announced that it would stage sit-ins at 510 locations across the country by blocking major roads. In a traffic advisory issued, the Karachi traffic police warned that traffic flow could be affected due to the protests and sit-ins, with slow-moving traffic, temporary diversions and partial road closures expected on several major thoroughfares. The affected areas included Mazar-i-Quaid, Numaish Chowrangi, Saddar, Sharea Faisal, Sharae Pakistan, UP Mor, Power House Chowrangi, Defence Housing Authority, Sea View, Shahrah-i-Orangi, Hub River Road, Super Highway and National Highway. The traffic police advised citizens to avoid travelling to the affected areas unless necessary, and urged them to select alternative routes and allow extra travel time before setting out. Meanwhile, according to the latest updates shared on JI Karachi’s official X account, party workers had begun staging sit-ins at the announced locations. According to the updates, workers had blocked the road leading to Natha Khan from Sharea Faisal. The Super Highway and Hub River Road were also blocked. Moreover, the road leading from Sharea Faisal Nursery Bus Stop to Airport had also been blocked. ‘Fuel for political point-scoring’ Responding to the protest, Sindh government spokesperson Sadia Javed said the petroleum levy was a federal matter and questioned why Karachi’s citizens were being “punished” through road closures. “Jamaat-i-Islami is using the protest to score political points instead of serving the public,” she alleged, adding that the party should focus on the performance of its local government representatives to improve conditions for Karachi’s residents. She said it was unacceptable for a few hundred protesters to hold a city of millions hostage by disrupting traffic and daily life, adding that such politics should come to an end. “Blocking roads does not serve the public; instead, it adds to their difficulties,” Javed said, questioning how ambulances and patients could reach hospitals when major roads were closed. “If Jamaat-i-Islami is sincere in its concerns, it should raise the matter at the relevant forums and in Parliament rather than resorting to protests that disrupt public life,” she said. Javed also warned that the party should not use Karachi’s residents as “fuel for political point-scoring” and stressed that authorities would not allow anyone to take the law into their own hands, block roads or damage public property under the guise of protest. Other parts of country Meanwhile, JI workers also gathered at the designated sit-in locations in other provincial capitals, including Lahore, Quetta, Peshawar and Islamabad. According to reports, Srinagar Highway had been blocked as protesters gathered at Golra Mor to march towards Chungi 26. In Sindh, protesters also staged sit-ins in Thatta, Matiari, Tando Allahyar, Shikarpur and other districts.

items.title: CAN féminine 2026 : Jorge Vilda veut qualifier le Maroc au Mondial face à l'Afrique du Sud
items.description: À la veille du quart de finale de la Coupe d'Afrique des nations féminine face à l'Afrique du Sud, le sélectionneur des Lionnes de l'Atlas, Jorge Vilda, a affiché sa confiance tout en insistant sur l'importance de cette rencontre, qui pourrait offrir au Maroc une qualification directe pour la Coupe du monde 2027. En conférence de presse ce vendredi, le technicien espagnol a assuré que ses joueuses étaient prêtes à relever le défi. « Nous avons une grande envie de gagner et une grande confiance. Nous voulons que le Maroc se qualifie directement pour la Coupe du monde pour la deuxième fois de son histoire. Nous voulons atteindre cet objectif dès demain », a déclaré Vilda. Le sélectionneur a toutefois appelé à la prudence face aux Banyana Banyana, championnes d'Afrique en titre. Selon lui, le staff technique connaît parfaitement les qualités de l'équipe sud-africaine, notamment sa vitesse et son jeu collectif. « Nous respectons beaucoup l'Afrique du Sud. Ce sera un match équilibré qui se jouera sur des détails. J'espère que ces détails seront en notre faveur. Aujourd'hui, nous abordons cette équipe avec respect, mais sans aucune crainte » , a-t-il souligné. Interrogé sur le manque d'efficacité offensive observé lors du dernier match face au Sénégal, où le Maroc s'était créé plus de vingt occasions sans parvenir à marquer, Jorge Vilda s'est montré rassurant. Le sélectionneur estime qu'il s'agit d'un problème ponctuel et se dit convaincu que ses joueuses retrouveront leur réalisme devant le but lors de cette rencontre décisive. Il a également mis en avant la solidité défensive de son équipe, qui n'a encaissé aucun but depuis le début de la compétition. Selon lui, cette performance est avant tout le fruit du travail collectif de l'ensemble du groupe et non uniquement des prestations de la gardienne. Enfin, Jorge Vilda a lancé un appel aux supporters marocains afin qu'ils viennent soutenir massivement les Lionnes de l'Atlas. « Nous avons besoin de nos supporters. Nous avons besoin de tous les Marocains, au stade comme devant leur télévision. Je suis convaincu que nous atteindrons notre objectif ensemble et j'espère que les joueuses entendront le rugissement du public plus fort que jamais » , a-t-il déclaré. Le Maroc affrontera l'Afrique du Sud ce samedi au stade Moulay El Hassan de Rabat, avec un double objectif : décrocher une place en demi-finales de la CAN féminine 2026 et valider sa qualification directe pour la Coupe du monde 2027 au Brésil. items.title: Agalga is tough but lacks leadership experience for Majority Leader role — Nitiwul
items.description: Former Defence Minister has said the Builsa North MP James Agalga who is the leading contender to become the next Majority Leader of Parliament, lacks the leadership experience required for his new role and must quickly adapt if he is to succeed in managing government business in Parliament. Speaking on The Pulse on JoyNews on Friday, August 7, while discussing President John Dramani Mahama’s recent reshuffle, Dominic Nitiwul said although Mr Agalga is a capable and resilient politician, leading the Majority Caucus demands experience that can only be acquired over time. “Agalga is a very tough, tough, tough guy. You know, he’s a very tough guy.” Mr Nitiwul, however, said toughness alone would not be enough to navigate the demands of parliamentary leadership. “The only thing he needs to realise is that he does not have the experience of leadership.” He explained that several senior Members of Parliament, including Minority Leader Alexander Afenyo-Markin, former Majority Chief Whip Frank Annoh-Dompreh, Patricia Appiagyei and Habib Iddrisu, had spent years in leadership positions and therefore possessed valuable experience. “Afenyo-Markin, Annoh-Dompreh, Patricia Appiagyei, and Habib have the experience of leadership. They have been there. All the four of them have been there long before him. Some of them have done seven years, six years. Some of them have done six and a half years.” According to Mr Nitiwul, leadership is not only a calling but also a skill that is developed through experience. “It is a calling. But apart from that, it is a skill that you need to learn on your feet.” He said that Mr Agalga entered Parliament around the same period as Mr Afenyo-Markin and therefore understands parliamentary procedure, adding that he was not surprised President Mahama selected him for the position. “When it comes to parliamentary work, Agalga came in, I think, 2012. So he came with Afenyo. They are mates. So he has an idea about how to go about leadership. So I’m not surprised that the president picked him to go.” Mr Nitiwul said he believed Mr Agalga would have been considered for the Defence Ministry if he had not been appointed Majority Leader. “If he didn’t go there, then he would have gone to Defence.” Despite expressing confidence in Mr Agalga’s ability, Mr Nitiwul cautioned that the new Majority Leader would have to settle into the role quickly or risk losing control of proceedings in the House. “He has to learn very fast. Otherwise, trust me, the mighty 87 will overrun him.” He warned that the Minority Caucus would take advantage of any weaknesses if Mr Agalga failed to establish himself. “If he’s not on his feet, the 87 will overrun him and overrun him very, very quickly.” Mr Nitiwul also commented on the departure of Mahama Ayariga as Majority Leader, saying the decision had long been expected within Parliament. “It was obvious to everybody that Mahama Ayariga would leave the front bench. It was very obvious before we left.” He said there had been widespread speculation that Mr Ayariga would be reassigned if changes were made to Cabinet. Read also: Mahama names Zanetor Rawlings for Environment, nominates Ayariga to Local Government in first reshuffle The former Defence Minister insisted that Mr Ayariga’s exit was not solely linked to his performance, revealing that there were other factors he could not publicly discuss. “There are some other reasons, which I cannot say on air, that he needed to leave. And it was in his interest to leave the front leadership.” He acknowledged that some members of the governing National Democratic Congress were dissatisfied with Mr Ayariga’s handling of parliamentary business, particularly his exchanges with Minority Leader Alexander Afenyo-Markin. “It’s not about performance or non-performance, even though the NDC party have their own issues with him. The way he went about things and the way he and Afenyo, in the exchanges and how he came out with, some of them felt unsatisfied with the way he went about things.” Mr Nitiwul, however, said the ultimate verdict on Mr Ayariga’s leadership would rest with the Ghanaian electorate. “That is for the jury to judge, and that jury will be the electorates in 2028.” Builsa North Member of Parliament James Agalga is the leading contender to become the next Majority Leader of Parliament following Mahama Ayariga’s appointment to President John Dramani Mahama’s cabinet, sources within the National Democratic Congress (NDC) Caucus have told MyJoyOnline .

items.title: Gunmen kidnap two farmers in Ondo, demand N100m ransom
items.description: …Police, Amotekun launch rescue operation By Dayo Johnson, Akure Suspected gunmen have abducted two farmers in Parubber Community, Ile-Oluji/Okeigbo Local Government Area of Ondo State, with the kidnappers reportedly demanding a ransom of N100 million for their release. A family source said the victims were ambushed on their farms on Monday and taken into a nearby forest by the assailants. One of the farmers who escaped the attack, Pastor Yemi Omowale, said the incident had been reported to the police and the Ondo State Security Network Agency, codenamed Amotekun. Omowale, who operates a piggery farm in Parubber Community along the Ondo-Ife Road, recounted the incident. “I run a piggery farm in Parubber Community along Ondo-Ife Road in Ile-Oluji/Okeigbo Local Government Area. We went there in the morning to feed the animals. “Between 12 noon and 1 p.m. on Monday, we were working outside when I saw a masked man carrying an AK-47 moving towards one of the victims, Adetan Adebanjo Gbemi, because we were not standing together,” he said. According to him, the abductors have contacted the wife of one of the victims and are demanding N100 million as ransom. “They have been calling the victim’s wife to ask how much she has been able to raise. We are appealing to the security agencies and the government to help rescue our brother and sister unharmed,” Omowale said. Confirming the incident, the spokesperson for the Ondo State Police Command, DSP Jimoh Abayomi, said the Oke-Igbo Divisional Headquarters received a report that the victims were missing. He said a joint security team comprising police operatives, including the Anti-Kidnapping Squad, Amotekun personnel, local hunters and vigilantes, had been deployed to the area. “Search and rescue operations are currently ongoing, with all available operational and intelligence resources being deployed to locate the victims and bring the perpetrators to justice,” Abayomi said. He added that efforts were being intensified to rescue the victims unharmed and apprehend those behind the abduction. The police spokesperson urged residents to remain calm and provide any credible information that could assist the ongoing operation through the nearest police formation. He reaffirmed the command’s commitment to securing the safe release of the victims and ensuring the suspects are brought to justice.
